REPORT DATE: 05-30-2022 REPORT TIME: 0130 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: SOUTH TIMBALIER 34 IMAGE DATE: 05-29-2022 IMAGE TIME: 2358 UTC DATA SOURCE: RADARSAT2 MODE: SCANSAR NARROW VV RESOLUTION: 25 METER LOCATION: 28°55"28" N/90°29"36" W AREA: 2.31 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH REMARKS: POSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THE SLICK EXTENDED AROUND 2.5 NM LONG BY ABOUT 0.5 NM WIDE AT ITS WIDEST POINT, HAD GOOD CONTRAST WITH ITS BACKGROUND AND HAD FEATHERING ON ITS TRAILING EDGE CONSISTENT WITH WSW WINDS AT 5 KT AT THE TIME OF THE IMAGE. THIS SLICK MAY BE RELATED TO AN NRC REPORT (#I1337274) ASSOCIATED WITH AN OIL RELEASE INTO THE GULF TO THE W OF THIS REPORT EARLIER TODAY, BUT THIS CANNOT BE CONFIRMED. CONSIDERING THE ABOVE FACTORS, WE HAVE MED-HIGH CONFIDENCE IN THIS ASSESSMENT. UNCERTAINTIES: THERE IS A SLIGHT POSSIBILITY THAT THE ANOMALY MAY BE SOMETHING OTHER THAN OIL, SUCH AS BIOGENIC MATTER. MAPS AND SHAPEFILES CAN BE ACCESSED AT: WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/

VOC AND BENZENE MONITORING STILL SHOWS NO DETECTION AT THE FENCE LINE. /// ORGINAL REPORT BELOW /// /// THIS IS AN UPDATE TO NRC REPORT #1324986 /// THE UPDATE IS AS FOLLOWS: THE CALLER STATED THAT ORIGINALLY THE RELEASE WAS BELIEVED TO BE SECURED AND ENDED, HOWEVER RESIDUE OMISSIONS OF BENZENE WERE DISCOVERED ABOVE THE FLOATING ROOF OF THE TANK. ADDITIONALLY THE SITE HAS PUT IN PLACE CORRECTIVE ACTIONS TO ADDRESS THE RESIDUAL ADMISSIONS AND CONTINUES TO EVALUATE ADDITIONAL CORRECTIVE ACTIONS. ACCORDING TO THE CALLER THE AMOUNT OF MATERIAL THAT RELEASED HAS BEEN CHANGED, WHICH IS REFLECTED IN THE RELEASED MATERIAL PAGE. properties.content:

Nearest City: Kent, WA
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: SOULTION CONTAINING NITRIC ACID AND HYDROFLOURIC ACID
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: GKN CHEM-TRONICS
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 200 gallons
CALLER REPORTED THAT A COUPLE BACKFLOW VALVES FAILED TURING THE SPARGER SYSTEM (AIR SYSTEM) INTO A SIPHON AND CAUSING A SOLUTION WHICH CONTAINS 45% NITRIC ACID AND ACID AND 4% HYDROFLOURIC ACID TO SPILL INTO A CONTAINMENT AREA. HOWEVER, AS THE MATERIAL TRAVELLED THROUGH THE PIPING SOME SEALS DETERIORATED ALLOWING 150-200 GALLONS OF SOLUTION TO SPILL INTO AN ALLEY BEHIND THE FACILITY AND INTO A STORM DRAIN LEADING TO MILL CREEK. NO MATERIAL IS BELEIVED TO HAVE REACHED MILL CREEK. THE FACILITY ITSELF AND THE SARA LEE BAKERY ADJACENT TO IT WERE EVACUATED AS A PRECAUTION, NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED.

Skytruth Analysis

INDIVIDUAL IS REPORTING AUXILIARY AVIATION FACILITY 7353E WAS FLYING A LONG ISLAND (NY) SOUTH SHORE PATROL ON WED., 26 DEC. 2007. AT 1055 LOCAL TIME, WHILE FLYING OVER THE SHINNECOCK INLET AT THE EAST END OF LONG ISLAND'S SOUTH SHORE WE OBSERVED A PETRO. SHEEN ON THE WATER OF THE SHINNECOCK BAY. THE SHEEN APPEARED TO BE COMING FROM THE VICINITY OF THE SOLEAU'S WHARF AND MARINA COMPLEX ON THE BAY SIDE JUST WEST OF THE INLET. THE F/V CINDISEA WAS DOCKED AT SOLEAU'S WEST DOCK AND THERE WAS A CONCENTRATION OF SHEEN NEAR THE VESSEL. IMMEDIATELY TO THE WEST OF THE CINDISEA THERE WAS A T DOCK WITH 2 F/V (THE PATRIOT AND THE MT SINAI) DOCKED AT THE END OF THE T. THERE WAS SOME SHEEN AROUND THOSE VESSELS ALSO. THE SHEEN WAS BEING CARRIED EAST BY THE OUTGOING TIDE TO THE INLET AND THEN OUT OF THE INLET INTO THE ATLANTIC OCEAN CREATING A LARGE FAN-LIKE PATTERN OUTSIDE THE INLET. THERE WERE SEALS AND BIRDS IN THE VICINITY OF THE SHEEN AND PEOPLE WERE SURFING OFF THE OCEAN BEACH ON THE WEST SIDE OF THE INLET. THE SHEEN WAS REPORTED TO USCG STA. SHINNECOCK AND USCG SECTOR LONG ISLAND SOUND (NEW HAVEN CT) BY MARINE RADIO. PHOTOS OF THE SHEEN WERE POSTED TO HOMEPORT ON THE USCG DISTRICT 1 INTELLIGENCE BRANCH COMMUNITY UNDER ANNOUNCEMENTS.
